 Aaron Gordon's Shooting Slump Challenges Denver Nuggets

 Denver's offensive balance faces another challenge as Aaron Gordon struggles to maintain his shooting efficiency ahead of the Nuggets' matchup against the Boston Celtics on Wednesday, November 18. The game is scheduled for 9:40 p.m. ET at Ball Arena in Denver, with Gordon's declining production becoming an increasingly important concern for the team.
 According to Nugglove, Gordon's overall performance has declined during the 2026-27 season, with his scoring, shooting efficiency, and defensive contributions falling below expectations. His physical playing style and history of injuries have also raised questions about his ability to maintain his previous level of athleticism.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 The most significant statistical change has come from beyond the three-point line. Gordon has converted just 27% of his attempts from three-point range this season, compared with 39% last season, when he attempted 4.4 shots per game from that distance.

 Celtics Name Starting Five for Nuggets Matchup in Denver 
 His overall field-goal percentage has also fallen from 50% last season to 40% this season. Nugglove reported that his shooting volume has remained similar, but fewer attempts are finding the basket.
 Denver previously benefited from Gordon's ability to contribute around the basket while stretching opposing defenses with reliable perimeter shooting. His role in the dunker spot and as a spot-up shooter has made him an important part of the offensive structure alongside Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray.
 However, the current shooting decline has reduced one of the team's important offensive options. Gordon had provided Denver with a combination of athleticism and perimeter shooting, two qualities that have become particularly important to the team's overall balance.
 Also Read 
 Jokic Demands Role Accountability After Nuggets Fall to Suns 
 According to statistics published by sports.betmgm.com, Gordon is averaging 11.0 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 1.2 three-pointers per game this season. His recent performance against the Phoenix Suns on November 16 included 11 points, one rebound, one assist, and two made three-pointers.
 His historical numbers against Boston offer a different perspective. Across 27 career appearances against the Celtics, Gordon has averaged 14.1 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game.
 His recent home performances against Boston have also produced notable results. Gordon averaged 17.0 points in his last two home appearances against the Celtics, alongside 4.0 assists during those games.

 Rebounding has been another productive area in his recent matchups. He averaged 8.3 rebounds across his last three appearances against Boston, while his career average against the franchise stands at 7.5 rebounds per game.
 His three-point production against the Celtics has been less consistent. Gordon averaged 1.0 made three-pointers across 27 career meetings and just 0.7 over his last three appearances against the team.
 Denver still has an opportunity to benefit from a turnaround, as the season remains in its early stages. However, Gordon's ability to recover his shooting efficiency will remain an important factor in maintaining the offensive balance built around Jokic, Murray, and the team's supporting players.
